title: Oscar and the Oath
premise: Bram Nystrom, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has spent a decade hiding among the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, trading in miracles she refuses to speak aloud. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark on the same night, Bram learns her guildmaster sold the covenant between realms to a rival power—and that her own oath was the keystone holding it together. Pursued by wardens who once were her sworn kin and drawn to Vess, a starless cartographer mapping the dying sky, Bram must choose between the silence that kept her safe and the voice that could save two worlds. In the end she reforges the covenant not with an oath but with a freely given promise, unbinding herself at the cost of her swordspeech, and chooses Vess and a small, ordinary life over the power that made her legend.
about_author: Bram Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing broken contracts in a northern university's rare books collection. They write fantasy about people trapped by their own promises, and claim every story begins with a clause someone didn't read carefully.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Miracles
chapters.summary: In Bram's POV, we see her quiet double life: cataloguing impossible trades by day, never speaking her swordspeech, never drawing her oath-blade. A routine entry—a bottled thunderstorm—goes wrong when the storm recognizes her name. The beat is uneasy comfort: safety that feels like suffocation.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Still Bram's POV. The border wards shatter and the stars extinguish in a single hour; the guildhouse shakes as clients flood in demanding answers. Guildmaster Corvane orders everyone inside and burns one ledger page before anyone can read it. The emotional beat is dread—the first crack in her hiding place.

chapters.title: A Cartographer of Nothing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV introduces Vess, who charts a sky that no longer exists, and whose maps show a wound where the stars should be. She seeks the guild to buy 'a way through the dark' and recognizes Bram's blade-oil scent from a massacre ten years past. The beat is wary attraction laced with old guilt.

chapters.title: What Corvane Sold
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Following the burned page's ash residue, she finds Corvane's hidden contract: he traded the covenant's keystone—an oath-speaker's living word—to the Hollow Court for the guild's survival. He offers Bram a choice: stay silent and be spared. The beat is betrayal sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Door
chapters.summary: Vess's POV as the Oathwardens arrive, led by Serrek, Bram's former shield-brother who believes she deserted the covenant and caused its fall. Vess lies to protect Bram without knowing why. The beat is loyalty tested by love that hasn't yet admitted its name.

chapters.title: The Road Through the Hollow
chapters.summary: Bram and Vess flee together toward the First Hearth where covenants are forged, crossing land eaten by the Hollow Court's silence—villages where no one remembers their own names. Bram nearly speaks her swordspeech to save a child and stops herself. The beat is intimacy forged in shared danger.

chapters.title: Serrek's Confession
chapters.summary: Serrek corners them; instead of a duel, he reveals the truth: the covenant was always powered by coerced oaths, and the wardens knew. He asks Bram to kill him rather than let him hunt her. She refuses, breaking his worldview. The beat is grief for a brotherhood built on a lie.

chapters.title: The Price of the Word
chapters.summary: At the First Hearth, Bram learns reforging the covenant demands an oath freely spoken—but any oath binds the speaker forever, as hers once did. Vess offers to take her place; Bram realizes loving Vess means refusing her sacrifice. The beat is love against duty made explicit and unbearable.

chapters.title: Covenant of Ash and Starlight
chapters.summary: Climax, Bram's POV. The Hollow Court arrives to claim its purchase; Corvane, seeking redemption, dies holding the door. Bram speaks—not an oath but a promise, offered and revocable—and the covenant accepts it because it is free. Her swordspeech burns away. The beat is triumph purchased with identity.

chapters.title: A Map With Two Names
chapters.summary: Resolution, alternating POV. Stars return, changed but steady; Vess charts a new sky and names a constellation after Bram's lost blade. Wardens become keepers rather than hunters. Bram, voice ordinary now, opens a small shop of possible things beside Vess. The beat is belonging chosen, not bound.
